newsitem.title: GERMANY: Computer 2000 US unit hit 9-month results.
newsitem.headline: Computer 2000 US unit hit 9-month results.

text.p: German computer distributor Computer 2000 AG said on Tuesday strong market growth in Europe had spurred a 23.4 percent rise in group sales in the first nine months of 1996/97 to 6.28 billion marks ($3.4 billion).
But it repeated its previous forecast that the ailing fortunes of its U.S. unit would mean losses for the full year.
"Because of the restructuring measures in the USA, we are counting on a negative result and a striking of the dividend," the company said in a letter to shareholders.

Viag AG, which owns 75 percent of Computer 2000, said earlier this month it planned to trim the operations of AmeriQuest Technologies Inc and sell off the loss-making computer distributor by the end of the year.

Computer 2000 told shareholders it has already sold off Ameriquest's CMS Enhancements Inc unit and cut staff and operations at its Advanced Systems Group, a distributor of computer workstations and servers based in Horsham, Pa.

In the nine-month period ending June 30, sales in Europe surged 27.5 percent to 5.67 billion marks, Computer 2000 said. Waning Ameriquest revenues caused foreign sales to fall 4.6 percent to 612 million marks.
Excluding AmeriQuest, the company said profit "clearly exceeded expectations."
Viag, a diversified utility, said on July 15 it had no plans to sell Computer 2000, and forecast a slight sales rise and stable or slightly higher earnings in 1997.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.836 German Marks)
